questions.question: Whom did Maria Vázsan, baptised 10 January 1853 at Bojnice (Bajmóc), Slovakia, daughter of Ignatius Vázsan and Anna Prividzer, marry?
questions.rationale: The marriage is the foundational fact the entire objective rests on. Maria's husband's identity, the marriage date, and the officiating parish determine where children would be recorded and which surname they would carry. Slovak Roman Catholic marriage registers for the Bojnice parish (Prievidza district) survive within the Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books collection on FamilySearch; given her 1853 baptism, a marriage in roughly 1870–1895 is the expected search window. Resolving the marriage is a prerequisite for the enumerative children question that follows.

items.jurisdiction: Bojnice (Bajmócz), Nyitra County, Kingdom of Hungary
items.rationale: The locality guide (loc_001) confirms that the Bojnice Roman Catholic marriage registers in the Slovakia, Church and Synagogue Books collection are not covered by the collection's digital name index and must be browsed image by image. DGS 5219331 contains a handwritten alphabetical marriage index for 1843–1876, enabling targeted lookup under the surname Vázsan (and variant spellings such as Vasán) without paging through every entry. Maria was born January 1853 and could plausibly have married from about 1870 onward, so this index covers the first half of her likely marriage window. Records are in Latin and Hungarian; consult the FamilySearch Latin and Hungarian Genealogical Word Lists and the Given Name Equivalents table for the Austro-Hungarian Empire when reading entries.

items.jurisdiction: Bojnice (Bajmócz), Nyitra County, Kingdom of Hungary
items.rationale: DGS 5219332 continues the alphabetical marriage index for 1877–1912, covering the later part of Maria's likely marriage window. Hungarian civil registration did not begin until 1895, so the parish register remains the sole contemporaneous marriage record before that date; after 1895 both civil and parish registers may exist. Browse the V section of this index for Vázsan entries, noting variant spellings in Latin and Hungarian. This item is browsed alongside item 2 as the second volume of the same alphabetical index series.

The Slovakia, Church and Synagogue Books collection (1554443) is name-searchable. Although the Bojnice marriage registers are not covered by the digital name index per loc_001, a broader name search for Vázsan and variant spellings across all indexed parishes may surface a partially indexed entry from Bojnice or from a neighbouring parish such as Prievidza where Maria could have married. Apply the Nyitra County filter and try all known spelling variants of the surname.

Contact details and guidance on written requests should be sought on the archive's official website; no specific postal address was returned by tools this session.

items.jurisdiction: Prievidza district, Nyitra County, Kingdom of Hungary
items.rationale: The Slovakia, Church and Synagogue Books collection (1554443) is name-searchable for baptism records — 14,391 baptisms are indexed for the Prievidza district, per loc_001. Children's baptism entries in this era name both parents. If Maria married after 1873 and had children in or near Bojnice, searching for baptisms where the mother's surname is Vázsan (and variants: Vazan, Vasán, Vazán) across the Prievidza district would return entries that name both Maria and her husband — indirectly revealing his surname and answering the marriage question. The DGS 5219332 image browse already confirmed the Bojnice baptism register 1877-1900 exists in this collection. Apply the Nyitra County / Prievidza district filter and use the mother's name as the primary search parameter. Date range 1874-1905 spans from the first plausible birth after a c.1873 marriage through the outer edge of a childbearing window for a woman born 1853.

items.rationale: If the targeted maternal Vázsan search in pli_008 yields nothing — perhaps because Maria consistently recorded her name under a spelling variant the mother-name index did not catch, or because she moved to a parish outside the indexed coverage — broaden to all Vázsan-surname baptism entries in the Prievidza district for the same period, regardless of whether Vázsan appears as the mother's name, the father's name, or a godparent. This surfaces the full family cluster: Maria's siblings and their children appear here too, and one of those baptism entries may list a godmother named Maria, point to a household under a different spelling, or otherwise place her. The Slovak naming tradition noted in loc_001 — first daughter often named Anna (after Maria's mother), first son often named Ignatius — provides a secondary check on which children are most likely hers.

# Locality Guide: Bojnice (Bajmócz), Prievidza District, Slovakia — formerly Nyitra County, Kingdom of Hungary (1850–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Historical name and county:** Bajmócz, Nyitra County (Nyitra vármegye), Kingdom of Hungary. The FamilySearch Catalog entry for the Roman Catholic parish (koha:1043283) explicitly identifies the historical jurisdiction as "Bajmócz, Nyitra, Hungary" — not Trenčín County.
- **Modern administrative home:** Bojnice, Prievidza district, Trenčín Region, Slovakia (since 1993)
- **Nearest administrative centre:** Prievidza (district seat today); historical county seat was Nyitra (modern Nitra, Slovakia)
- **Population during period:** Population data for Bojnice was not returned by the tools. The settlement is described as a historical town on the Nitra River near Prievidza with a current population of approximately 5,000.
- **Economy:** Agricultural settlement adjacent to Bojnice Castle; the surrounding Prievidza/Handlová basin was developing as a coal-mining region by the late 19th century
- **Ethnic and linguistic composition:** Predominantly Slovak-speaking population under Hungarian state administration; Catholicism was the dominant faith
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (with a parish of documented continuous existence from at least 1668)
- **Key historical events:** The 1867 Austro-Hungarian Compromise accelerated Magyarization; records shifted toward Hungarian. Church records were declared state property in 1784 (Joseph II); after 1949 they were nationalized and transferred to state regional archives.

## Boundary changes
- **1850–1918:** Bojnice (Bajmócz) was in Nyitra County, Kingdom of Hungary — not Trenčín County
- **1918:** Creation of Czechoslovakia; Slovak lands pass to Czechoslovak administration
- **1945/1949:** Church vital records nationalized; Bojnice registers transferred to the Štátny oblastný archív v Nitre (State Regional Archive in Nitra)
- **1993:** Independent Slovakia; Bojnice placed in Prievidza district, Trenčín Region
- Note: The county boundary matters. Searching for civil or county-level records under "Trenčín" will not find Nyitra County material. Use "Nyitra" or "Nitra" when searching historical catalogues and indexes.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** National civil registration in the Kingdom of Hungary began in 1895, per the FamilySearch Slovakia Civil Registration wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Slovakia_Civil_Registration). For 1850–1895, the Catholic parish registers are the only source.
- **What exists for 1895–1900:** State civil birth, marriage, and death registers from 1895 onward. These are not confirmed to be available online for Bojnice.
- **Where held:** Local civil registration offices (matričné úrady) hold records not yet transferred to state archives; older transferred material is at the Štátny oblastný archív v Nitre.

### Church records
- **Parish:** Rímsko-katolícka cirkev. Farský úrad Bojnice (Roman Catholic Parish Office, Bojnice). Catalog ID: koha:1043283.
- **Coverage:** Baptisms, marriages, deaths, confirmations, conversions, illegitimate births, and mixed marriages 1668–1912. All five digitized films are available online through the Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books collection (https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1554443).
- **Films covering 1850–1900 (all marked Online and Indexed Y in the catalog):**
  - DGS 5219331 (film 2236106): Baptisms 1840–1876 (with alphabetical index 1865–1876); Marriages 1777–1866 (with alphabetical index 1777–1842); Deaths 1777–1833
  - DGS 5219332 (film 2236107): Marriages 1866–1912 with alphabetical indexes for both 1843–1876 and 1877–1912; Baptisms 1877–1900 with alphabetical index 1877–1900; Death index 1834–1876; Deaths 1834–1876
  - DGS 5219333 (film 2236108): Deaths 1877–1906
- **Access level:** Despite the catalog marking Indexed Y, the volume_search tool returned 0% name-indexed for the Bojnice death volume found. Bojnice also does not appear in the FamilySearch indexed coverage table for the Prievidza district. Treat marriage and death registers as browse-only; the alphabetical indexes within each volume (listed above) are the practical search tool.
- **Originals held at:** Štátny oblastný archív v Nitre
- **Language:** Hungarian, Latin, and German

### Census records
- **1869 Hungarian census:** FamilySearch collection 1986782 — 278,392 images, browse-only, no name index. This enumeration could document the Vázsan family at Bojnice around Maria's childhood.
- **Access:** Free at FamilySearch; must be browsed image by image. See also the browsable index at http://www.iabsi.com/gen/public/CensusMain.htm#1869Census%7CSlovakia and the Jewish genealogy index at http://www.jewishgen.org/databases/Hungary/Census1869.htm.
- **Other enumerations:** No additional census collections for Bojnice in this period were returned by the FamilySearch tools.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, guardianships, inventories — county-level under Nyitra County, Hungarian administration
- **Where held:** No probate collections for Bojnice were returned by the FamilySearch tools. Consult the State Regional Archive in Nitra, which holds Nyitra County records.
- **Note:** A zero result from the catalog is a cataloguing gap, not evidence that records do not exist.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds, standard in the Kingdom of Hungary
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Nyitra County administration in the target period
- **Where held:** No land record collections for Bojnice were returned by the FamilySearch tools. Consult the Slovakia Land and Property wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Slovakia_Land_and_Property) and the Štátny oblastný archív v Nitre.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Austro-Prussian War (1866), ongoing Austro-Hungarian Imperial Army service throughout the period
- **Record types:** Military conscription lists and service records for men of the region
- **Where held:** See the curated guides: "Guide for Locating Military Records for the various Regions of the Austro-Hungarian Empire" (http://www.iabsi.com/gen/public/ahm.html) and "Military Records in Upper Hungary" (http://www.iabsi.com/gen/public/military_records_in_upper_hungar.htm). No specific FamilySearch collection for Bojnice military records was identified.

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** Three Slovakia-wide virtual cemetery databases are in the curated external links: Virtual Cemeteries of Slovakia (http://www.cemetery.sk/english/), Virtuálne cintoríny Slovenska (https://www.virtualnycintorin.sk/), and Slovenské cintoríny (https://www.slovenskecintoriny.sk/). Coverage for Bojnice specifically was not confirmed.
- **Parish burial registers:** Deaths 1834–1876 and 1877–1906 are in the Bojnice RC collection at FamilySearch. These records include date of death, name, age, residence, cause of death, and sometimes surviving relatives.

### Newspaper records
- **Online access:** MyHeritage Slovakia Newspapers from OldNews.com (https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-11038/slovakia-newspapers-from-oldnewscom) — subscription required. No Bojnice-specific local newspaper was identified by the tools.
- **Content value:** Hungarian-era newspapers carried marriage announcements, death notices, and legal notices; useful for families of higher social standing.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Hamburg was the primary departure port for emigrants from Upper Hungary (Slovakia) in the late 19th century.
- **Record types:** Hamburg Passenger Lists 1850–1934 (Ancestry, https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=1068); Hamburg Passenger Lists Handwritten Indexes 1855–1934 (Ancestry, https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=1166); Hamburg Emigrants at FindMyPast (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/hamburg-germany-emigrants).
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest page for all family members when researching a family group.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property and poll taxes at the county level (Nyitra County) under Hungarian administration
- **Where held:** No tax record collections for Bojnice were returned by the FamilySearch tools. Consult the Štátny oblastný archív v Nitre for Nyitra County tax lists.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists can partially substitute for missing census years.

### Other record types
- **Confirmations:** The Bojnice RC parish registers include confirmation records (Birmovaní); these provide a second dated event for an individual, typically several years after baptism.
- **Illegitimate births and mixed marriages:** These are recorded separately within the parish registers; the catalog notes these series exist for Bojnice.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Slovakia Church and Synagogue Books 1592–1935 (collection 1554443) — Bojnice RC parish registers 1668–1912; Slovakia Census 1869 (collection 1986782) | Free |
| MyHeritage | Slovakia, Church and Synagogue Books, 1592–1910 (https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30139/slovakia-church-synagogue-books-1592-1910) | Subscription |
| Ancestry | Slovakia, Church and Synagogue Books, 1592–1910 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60146) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** The volume_search tool returned 1 digitized volume for Bojnice in the 1850–1900 window — a browse-only death index (1834–1876, DGS 005219332_004_M99X-H72, 108 images). The FamilySearch Catalog (koha:1043283) is the authoritative finding aid and shows five film rolls online, covering baptisms, marriages, deaths, and confirmations 1668–1912. ## Known record losses
No tool result reported destruction of Bojnice parish records for the 1850–1900 period. The FamilySearch Slovakia Church Records wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Slovakia_Church_Records) notes that some earlier Slovak church books were lost during Turkish invasions and upheavals around 1600–1700, but the Bojnice registers begin in 1668, suggesting they survived that era. The 1850–1900 registers appear intact based on the catalog coverage.

## Research tips
- **Browse the alphabetical marriage indexes before scrolling the full registers.** The FamilySearch Trenčín Region Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Trenčín_Region_(Trenčiansky_kraj),_Slovakia_Genealogy) confirms that marriage registers are not name-indexed in the searchable collection. However, the Bojnice parish films include alphabetical marriage indexes within the volumes: index 1843–1876 and index 1877–1912 in DGS 5219332. Browse those indexes first for the marriage entry.
- **Use both the Hungarian and Slovak place name when navigating FamilySearch.** The Slovakia Church Records wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Slovakia_Church_Records) recommends searching by the parish town name in both Slovak (Bojnice) and Hungarian (Bajmócz or Bajmoc). The Genealogy Slovakia Gazetteer (http://www.cisarik.com/0_all-villages-A.html) lists all name forms and confirms the historical county.
- **Pre-1895 records are in Latin or Hungarian.** The Trenčín Region wiki notes that pre-1918 records may be in Hungarian, Latin, German, or Slovak. For this Catholic parish in the second half of the 19th century, expect Latin in earlier decades and Hungarian becoming dominant after 1867. Use the FamilySearch Hungarian and Latin Genealogical Word Lists.
- **Look for given names in their Latin or Hungarian form.** The Slovakia Naming Customs wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Slovakia_Naming_Customs) notes that names were recorded in the language of the priest. 'Maria' may appear as Mariae (Latin) or Mária (Hungarian); 'Ignatius' as Ignatz or Ignác. Use the Given Name Equivalents table at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Given_Name_Equivalents_in_the_Austro-Hungarian_Empire to identify all forms.
- **Naming tradition can help confirm which children are Maria's.** The Slovakia Naming Customs wiki states it was traditional in rural Slovak communities to name the first child of each sex after the corresponding grandparent. If this pattern was followed, knowing Maria's parents were Ignatius and Anna may help identify her children in the baptism registers.
- **If Bojnice records are incomplete, search the Prievidza RC parish.** The Trenčín Region wiki advises searching neighbouring parishes when an ancestor cannot be found. Prievidza, the nearest town, had its own RC parish; families near the parish boundary may have records at either church.
